newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy gives ENI share pricing details.
newsitem.headline: Italy gives ENI share pricing details.

text.p: The Italian Treasury announced on Saturday that the second tranche of shares in energy giant ENI offered to investors would give private buyers at least a 3.5 percent discount to the closing share price on Friday October 25.

In previous reports, Reuters erroneously said the price for private investors was at a discount to the price offered to institutions and that a maximum price quoted by the Treasury related to institutional purchasers rather than private buyers.
Subsequent Reuter reports carried these erroneous references.
The ENI share price closed down 0.45 percent at 7,464 lire on Monday.
The Treasury also added in a statement on Saturday that the maximum price that private investors will have to pay has been set at 7,425 lire per share.
Retail investors will be offered ENI shares at either the 3.5 percent discount to the closing share price on October 25 or the maximum of 7,425 lire, whichever is the lower.
The statement said the second tranche placement of about 700 million shares would bring the Treasury's stake in ENI to around 76 percent from 85 percent.

Of the total number of shares, some 300 million shares are being offered to Italian retail investors, 235 million shares to institutional investors and 165 million shares to investors in the United States.

Global coordinators for the sale, Italian investment bank IMI and CS First Boston, have been granted an over-allotment or "green-shoe" option of a further 105 million shares which will be offered to institutional investors in the case of heavy demand.
The Treasury has said the offer, which accounts for 8.75 percent of ENI's share capital, or 10 percent if the green shoe is included, could be increased if demand was strong enough.
Market expectations are for a share offer price of around 7,200-7,300 lire, putting a value of 5.8 trillion lire on the share offer.
In November 1995, the Treasury sold a first 15 percent tranche of ENI shares at 5,250 lire a share to trade in Milan London and New York, which raised 6.3 trillion lire.
The Italian public sale of the shares will run from October 21 to October 25 and the final share price will be fixed on October 26 and trading is expected to start on October 28.
ENI shares hit a year high on July 2 of 7,925 lire, and on Friday closed up 0.77 percent at 7,498 lire.
